results.title: Authentication
results.snippet:
Learn how to authenticate requests to the MrScraper API using API tokens and request headers.
The MrScraper API uses API token authentication to secure all endpoints. Every request must include a valid API token in the HTTP request headers.
## Getting Your API Token
API tokens are managed directly from your MrScraper dashboard.
Click **New Token**.
Enter a descriptive **token name** and choose an **expiration date**.
Click **Create**, then copy and securely store the generated token.
Keep Your Token Secure
## Authenticating Requests
Include your API token in the `x-api-token` HTTP header on every request:
```
x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```
### Marketplace Endpoints
For [Marketplace endpoints](https://app.mrscraper.com/marketplace), authenticate using the standard RFC 6750 `Authorization` header with a Bearer token:
```
Authorization: Bearer <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>
```
## Verify Token
To test your authentication and confirm that your token is valid, make a request to the [`/subscription-accounts`](***REDACTED*** endpoint:
```
curl -X GET "https://api.app.mrscraper.com/api/v1/subscription-accounts" \
-H "accept: application/json" \
-H "x-api-token: <MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN>"
```

results.snippet:
Most teams use one of two patterns:
1. **Your backend owns the key.** Your server holds a MrScraper API token. The agent calls your tools, and your server calls MrScraper.
2. **Each user connects their own account.** A person signs in to MrScraper through their MCP client, such as Claude Code or Codex. The client handles the sign-in, and the agent uses that person's access. The next section covers when to use each one.
## **When should you use API keys or OAuth?**
| Use an API key when | Use OAuth when |
|---|---|
| Your app calls MrScraper on its own behalf | A person connects their own MrScraper account |
| The call runs on your server, a job runner or CI | The call runs from that person's MCP client |
| One account pays for and owns the usage | Each person's usage should stay on their account |
| You control where the key is stored | You do not want anyone to copy or paste a key |

Use MrScraper's HTTP APIs from an AI agent or application and pay per request in USDC through [Circle Gateway](https://developers.circle.com/gateway-nanopayments). Buyers do not need a MrScraper API key or session cookie.
The integration exposes two services:
- **scraperAPI** retrieves a public page as rendered HTML, Markdown, a screenshot, or a combination of these outputs.
- **webSearch** searches Google with region, language, and pagination controls for web discovery, research, and SEO analysis.
## Endpoints and pricing
Base URL: `https://api.mrscraper.com/circle`
| Service | Method and path | Price per request |
|---|---|---|
| scraperAPI | `POST /api/mrscraper/scraperAPI` | **0.01 USDC** |
| webSearch | `POST /api/mrscraper/webSearch` | **0.01 USDC** |
Both endpoints accept and return `application/json`. Each search-results page is a separate request. Upstream fields such as `token_usage` and `tokenUsage` describe MrScraper plan usage; they are separate from the x402 USDC price.

results.title: @mrscraper/mcp
results.snippet:
MrScraper MCP is the official [MrScraper](https://mrscraper.com) server for the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). It connects AI assistants to page content and Google search through two SDK-compatible tools, plus an account check. Retrieve HTML, Markdown, or screenshots with `scraperAPI`, discover pages with `webSearch`, and check your plan and token usage with `status`.
Use the hosted server with OAuth sign-in, or run the open-source server locally with the [`@mrscraper/mcp` npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mrscraper/mcp). See the [MrScraper MCP documentation](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server) for setup instructions and client configurations.
The server exposes three tools:
```
scraperAPI  webSearch  status
```
## Deployment options
| Option | Endpoint or command | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Hosted | `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` | A managed Streamable HTTP connection |
| Local HTTP | `TRANSPORT=http npx -y @mrscraper/mcp@latest` | A self-managed HTTP service |
| Local stdio | `npx -y @mrscraper/mcp@latest` | MCP clients that launch a local process |

results.title: Use MrScraper MCP to Compare Public SaaS Pricing and Plan Limits
results.snippet:
An MCP SaaS pricing comparison uses an AI client, such as Claude Code, to collect official pricing and help pages through MrScraper's MCP tools. The client then turns each page into structured, cited rows. You compare plans only where units match, and you mark every unpublished price or limit as unknown.

Connect MrScraper's hosted MCP server to your AI client, then ask the client to call `scraperAPI` on each approved URL and extract facts into your schema. Each call returns the page content in the same response. Check the response before you trust any fact taken from it.
### **scraperAPI output and response validation**
MrScraper documents a hosted MCP endpoint at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` with OAuth 2.1 sign-in. In Claude Code, add it like this:
bash
```bash
claude mcp add \
--transport http \
--scope user \
mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```
Open `/mcp` in Claude Code to sign in. Other clients, including Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code, use the same URL. The [MrScraper MCP documentation](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server) lists the setup for each one.
